messages.content: Predict a human participant’s decision in two paid games. All amounts are US cents. Participants are separate real MTurk workers, and decisions are collected separately and matched afterwards. In Game A, Player 1 starts with 50 cents and Player 2 with nothing. Player 1 can keep 25 and give 25, or keep 45 and give 5. Player 3 starts with 50 cents and submits a conditional investment costing any integer from 0 to 45 cents. It is implemented if Player 1 makes the unfair 45/5 allocation. Each cent spent to punish subtracts one cent from Player 1’s 45-cent bonus, leaves Player 2’s 5 cents unchanged, and costs Player 3 one cent. The participant is assigned a helping or punishment condition. In Game B, one of two Player 3 workers is either randomly selected or chosen by Player 4. Player 4 starts with a new 30 cents, keeps any part not sent, and sends an integer S from 0 to 30 cents to the selected Player 3. Player 3 receives 3S cents and can return part or all of this money, keeping the rest. If R cents is returned, Player 3 keeps 3S−R and Player 4 receives 30−S+R. The return decision is not revealed to Player 4 when choosing a partner or sending money. Both roles receive a separate 50-cent participation fee. Player 4 sees both candidates’ Game A investments and chooses one partner. The current decision and its consequences are not yet known. Earlier answers below are the participant’s own responses to comprehension questions, completed before the decisions. Predict which of the two Player 3 workers Player 4 chooses. Identify candidates by their earlier investment: output only lower_investor or higher_investor.
